Job Summary The Technical Specialist supports the administration, maintenance, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement of enterprise physical security technology systems. This role provides day-to-day technical and operational support for access control, video management, identity management, badging, and related security platforms across multiple company locations. The successful candidate will work closely with Security, IT, Facilities, vendors, contractors, and site stakeholders to support system operations, resolve issues, maintain accurate security data, assist with project execution, and promote compliance with company security standards and processes. This position requires strong technical aptitude, attention to detail, customer service skills, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced enterprise security technology environment. Position Overview Your responsibilities may include: Support daily administration of enterprise security technology platforms, including Genetec Security Center, ClearID, Volt AI, access control systems, video management systems, badging systems, and related applications. Assist with cardholder, identity, credential, access rule, door, area, schedule, and permission updates. Utilize the Genetec ClearID REST API to automate cardholder data creation, enrichment, updates, and lifecycle management processes, enabling streamlined identity administration and enhanced service delivery to customers. Troubleshoot access control issues, including failed badge reads, inactive credentials, access rule conflicts, door configuration issues, and synchronization problems. Review and validate system data to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with company security standards. Support identity lifecycle activities for employees, contractors, and visitors, including badge access, expiration dates, account status, and access remediation. Assist with access reviews, supervisor verification processes, and cleanup of outdated or inaccurate access assignments. Support video system operations, including camera troubleshooting, recording issues, video access, coverage validation, and coordination of repairs. Maintain and update security technology records, including doors, cameras, panels, controllers, card readers, credentials, and other system assets. Coordinate with vendors, contractors, IT, Facilities, and site Security teams to support hardware repairs, replacements, installations, and system upgrades. Assist with security technology projects, migrations, deployments, testing, commissioning, and post-implementation support. Prepare reports, spreadsheets, summaries, and data extracts related to access activity, system issues, hardware inventories, project status, and compliance reviews. Document troubleshooting steps, findings, resolutions, and system changes in accordance with team standards. Support audit requests, evidence collection, data validation, and remediation tracking related to security technology systems. Provide clear, timely, and professional communication to users, supervisors, stakeholders, and management regarding system issues, access concerns, and required actions. Identify opportunities to improve security technology processes, system configuration, data quality, and operational efficiency. Basic Requirements: Legally authorized to work in the Unites States. Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Engineering or related field. Genetec technical certification in Omnicast and Synergis. 3 or more years of experience with Genetec solutions, including system implementation, data integration, application integration, data engineering, and other security technology disciplines, supporting the deployment, optimization, and continuous improvement of Genetec-based solutions. Working knowledge of access control concepts, including cardholders, credentials, doors, areas, schedules, access rules, and permissions. Experience troubleshooting technical issues and documenting findings, actions taken, and resolution details. Proficiency with Application Development (Python, C#, PowerShell) and Database Administration (SQL Server, SSMS, MySql) tools. Preferred Requirements: Ability to analyze system data, identify inconsistencies, and recommend corrective actions. Strong customer service, organizational, and communication skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities and work with technical and non-technical stakeholders. Experience with Genetec Security Center, Synergis, Omnicast, ClearID, Volt AI or similar enterprise physical security platforms. Experience with access control hardware such as Mercury controllers, HID readers, badge printers, door hardware, or related security devices. Experience with video management systems, IP cameras, camera troubleshooting, and recording system validation. Familiarity with identity governance, role-based access, access reviews, supervisor verification, and contractor badge expiration processes. Experience supporting enterprise security technology projects, migrations, hardware refreshes, or system deployments. Experience working with IT ticketing systems and coordinating issue resolution with internal teams and vendors. Strong analytical skills with the ability to work with reports, spreadsheets, system exports, and large data sets. Demonstrated ability to work independently, take ownership of assigned tasks, and follow issues through resolution. Ability to communicate technical information in a clear and professional manner to business users, site personnel, and leadership. Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Position - Sr Game Designer (Progression & Economy)

Haven Studios is a game development studio headquartered in Montreal. In May 2021, we embarked on a journey to start Haven as a small team with big ambitions. Our goal was to build a studio of exceptional people where together we could make the kind of games we’ve always wanted to create – games we’ve longed to play. At Haven, we believe that kindness, adaptability and fearless optimism make space for creative excellence. We are a hybrid studio that supports flexibility, focus and collaboration for our teams.

Haven joined the PlayStation Studios family as the first Sony game development team in Canada in 2022. Our first game is in development for PlayStation and PC, a competitive multiplayer action heist game with a vision to entertain and engage players for years to come.

Position - Sr Game Designer (Progression & Economy)

We are looking for an experienced Senior Game Designer with a highly structured, analytical mindset to own the progression systems, player lifecycle, and economic health of our upcoming live service title. In this role, you will design the frameworks that keep players engaged for years, translating high-level creative vision into mathematically sound, highly structured progression loops and economy systems. You will operate within a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment, ensuring that player investment, rewards, and monetization strategies feel cohesive, fair, and deeply engaging.

Reporting Line

The Senior Game Designer will report to the Project Lead-Game Design

Role and Responsibilities

• System Architecture: Design, model, and maintain complex player progression frameworks, monetization loops, and virtual economies that support long-term player retention and engagement in a live service environment.
• Structured System Design: Translate abstract player experience goals into precise structural maps, detailed spreadsheets, data tables, and algorithmic logic models.
• Balancing & Tuning: Own the balancing, pacing, and tuning of player rewards, XP curves, drop rates, sink/source mechanics, and overall game economy to eliminate inflation or progression bottlenecks.
• Live Service Integration: Coherently integrate progression, monetization, and social layers within a multiplayer AAA ecosystem, aligning features across both PvE and PvP dimensions.
• Cross-Functional Alignment: Act as the primary point of contact for progression and economy systems, working closely with Directors, Producers, Data Analysts, and Engineers to ensure structural feasibility and data telemetry readiness.
• Lifecycle Optimization: Adapt and optimize systems post-launch based on player metrics, behavior patterns, and shifting market trends while maintaining structural balance with new content releases.

Required Experience and Skills

• AAA Live Service Background: Extensive experience in systems or progression design with at least one shipped AAA multiplayer live service title where you owned or significantly contributed to the game's economy or progression loops.
• Structured Thinking: A proven, highly methodical approach to design. You rely on strong mathematical logic, complex spreadsheets, and structural documentation over guesswork.
• Economic Mastery: Deep understanding of macro and micro-economy principles in modern gaming, including monetization strategies, virtual currencies, reward pacing, and incentive loops.
• Engine Proficiency: Strong ability to work directly within the Unreal Engine editor to hook up data structures, configure data tables, and test progression parameter changes locally.
• Data-Informed Approach: Strong competence in interpreting live telemetry, player cohorts, A/B testing data, and macroeconomic analytics to guide balance adjustments and systems optimization.
• Clear Documentation: Exceptional ability to distill complex, multi-layered economic dependencies into clear, highly readable system specifications for technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Assets

• System Modeling Tools: Experience using economy simulation software or advanced mathematical scripting (e.g., Python, Machinations, or specialized spreadsheet modeling) to stress-test systems before implementation.
• Dual Discipline Background: Prior design experience crossing into complementary fields such as Level Design, Business Intelligence, Data Analytics, or UX Design.

GE Vernova is a world leader in energy, dedicated to electrifying the world while simultaneously working to decarbonize it. Our Consulting Services team provides global expertise to external clients and internal business units across the entire spectrum of power generation, delivery, and utilization. We specialize in complex power system studies, including shunt and series compensation, FACTS, HVDC, synchronous condensers, STATCOMs, and advanced dynamic controls for the modern grid.

Job Description

The Role

You will leverage your technical expertise to solve complex power system challenges, providing actionable insights that drive grid reliability and renewable integration.

Essential Responsibilities

• Technical Leadership: Lead complex transmission system studies, including load flow, short-circuit, stability, and voltage analysis.
• Grid Modernization: Support the integration of renewable energy and battery storage, evaluating grid code compliance and system impact for bulk power networks.
• Modeling & Simulation: Perform detailed electromagnetic transient (EMT) and steady-state studies; develop advanced user-defined equipment models.
• Client Engagement: Lead proposal development and client communications. Translate complex technical findings into clear, value-driven reports and executive presentations.

• Collaboration: Foster a culture of quality, innovation, and teamwork within a global, cross-functional environment.

• Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering (Power Systems focus) or related field.

• Solid understanding of inverter-based resource (IBR) control systems and familiarity with Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) standards (e.g., PJM, CAISO, ERCOT, MISO, SPP).

• Willingness to travel (up to 20%) to support project work, client meetings, and industry conferences.

• Advanced experience in developing/modifying dynamic user-defined models in PSS®E, PSLF, or PSCAD.

• Demonstrated ability to apply complex mathematics to real-world power system stability problems.

ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s API Multicloud team is responsible for extending OpenAI’s API platform into strategic cloud environments, starting with AWS https://openai.com/index/openai-on-aws/. The team is focused on bringing core developer and enterprise capabilities into cloud-native environments, including AWS-hosted Codex, model customization / post-training as a service, and new stateful runtime environments for agentic workloads. This work sits at the intersection of production ML systems, developer platforms, model behavior, and large-scale infrastructure.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring Machine Learning Engineers to build and improve the AI systems that help strategic partners adapt OpenAI models to important use cases in cloud-native environments. This role spans post-training workflows, evaluation, data pipelines, model behavior, and API/infrastructure integration.

You’ll work at the boundary between partner needs and core ML systems: helping teams understand what is and isn’t working, diagnosing issues in training and evaluation workflows, and turning those learnings into improvements to the underlying platform. You should enjoy working with external technical partners, extracting the real goal from messy requests, and pushing back or reframing when the requested experiment is not the highest-leverage path. You’ll collaborate closely with Research, Applied, Safety Systems, infrastructure teams, and external technical partners to solve ambiguous model-performance problems. When you succeed, strategic partners and internal teams will be able to improve model behavior with confidence, driving measurable product improvements while the systems behind that work become more reliable, scalable, and effective over time.

- Partner with strategic customers and internal teams to define target model behaviors, diagnose failure modes, and translate real-world needs into training, evaluation, and system requirements.

We are hiring a Security Software Engineer to design and implement the hardware-backed security foundations used across OpenAI’s device ecosystem.

A central focus of this role is hardening the boundary between our policy systems and the HSMs that protect sensitive cryptographic keys. This boundary determines which operations may be performed, what may be signed, which policies must be satisfied, and how changes to trusted software and policy are authorized.

You will develop security-critical software and firmware within, or immediately adjacent to, an HSM trust boundary. Depending on your background, this may include HSM trusted applications, firmware services, cryptographic mechanisms, device drivers, PKCS#11 components, secure-provisioning protocols, or signing-policy enforcement systems.

This is a hands-on software-engineering role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review production code, debug across hardware and software boundaries, and carry projects from initial requirements through deployment. It is not an HSM administration, PKI operations, compliance, or architecture-only position.

In This Role, You Will

- Design and implement security-critical software and firmware for HSMs, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and hardware roots of trust.

- Build and harden the policy-to-HSM boundary responsible for authorizing certificate issuance and cryptographic signing operations.

- Develop HSM trusted applications, firmware components, host interfaces, device drivers, SDKs, or cryptographic service integrations.

- Implement or extend cryptographic interfaces such as PKCS#11, OpenSSL providers or engines, platform key-storage APIs, or comparable hardware-security interfaces.

- Build firmware and software that cryptographically enforces key generation, provisioning, usage, rotation, recovery, and destruction policies.

- Design and implement HSM-backed certificate authority, code-signing, key-management, and device-identity systems.

- Develop end-to-end cryptographic protocols spanning devices, secure hardware, policy services, and backend infrastructure.

- Build security capabilities supporting device attestation, secure boot, factory provisioning and restoration, user registration, and authentication.

- Design controls that make trusted software and policy changes verifiable, auditable, and subject to appropriate multi-party authorization.

- Write, review, test, and audit secure embedded software for resource-constrained environments.

- Develop test harnesses, emulators, fuzzers, and fault-injection tooling to validate security properties and failure behavior.

- Threat-model hardware and software trust boundaries and translate findings into concrete engineering improvements.

- Partner with hardware, firmware, infrastructure, application, and security teams to integrate secure-by-default capabilities into production systems.

- Help establish engineering standards for HSM development, applied cryptography, secure key management, and certificate infrastructure.

Minimum Qualifications

- 5+ years experience building secure embedded firmware for constrained environments

- Deep programming experience in C, C++, or Rust.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

- A strong track record of designing, implementing, debugging, and shipping production systems software.

- Hands-on experience developing security-critical software or firmware within, or directly adjacent to, an HSM, secure element, TEE, or hardware root of trust.

- Experience developing one or more of the following:

- HSM firmware or trusted applications

- Cryptographic mechanisms or hardware-accelerated cryptographic services

- HSM device drivers, host libraries, SDKs, or middleware

- PKCS#11 providers, mechanisms, or integrations

- Secure key-provisioning or key-injection protocols

- HSM-backed certificate authority or code-signing systems

- Signing-policy enforcement within a hardware-backed trust boundary

- Strong knowledge of applied cryptography, digital signatures, key hierarchies, secure key management, and cryptographic protocol design.

- Experience with PKI, X.509 certificates, certificate authorities, certificate issuance, and certificate lifecycle protocols.

- Familiarity with secure boot, measured boot, device identity, remote attestation, or hardware-backed storage.

- Experience reasoning about concurrency, memory safety, privilege separation, hardware interfaces, failure modes, and side-channel or physical attack considerations.

- The ability to evaluate security designs and personally implement the software required to realize them.

- Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate across hardware, firmware, backend, and product teams.

Additional Experience That May Be Helpful

- Firmware development for ARM TrustZone or another trusted execution environment.

- Experience with commercial or cloud HSM platforms such as Thales Luna, Entrust/nShield, Utimaco, Marvell LiquidSecurity, AWS CloudHSM, or comparable systems.

- Experience with PKCS#11, KMIP, OpenSSL providers or engines, secure-element APIs, or platform-native key-storage frameworks.

- Device manufacturing, secure provisioning, factory restore, or silicon bring-up experience.

- Secure boot ROM, bootloader, firmware-signing, anti-rollback, or authenticated-update development.

- Developing trusted applications or cryptographic services inside an HSM or secure coprocessor.

- Hardware/software co-design involving cryptographic accelerators, secure processors, or custom silicon.

- Multi-party authorization, quorum-controlled deployments, tamper-resistant audit mechanisms, or attestable policy systems.

- Secure or private storage systems based on hardware-protected keys.

- Experience sustaining high-assurance security software in production.

About the Team

GTM Growth Engineering builds AI-native products that help OpenAI's go-to-market and B2B marketing organizations scale with greater speed, intelligence, and operational effectiveness.

We apply OpenAI models to real business workflows and build the systems that make those applications useful and dependable: customer context, agent behavior, feedback, evaluation, experimentation, and appropriate human oversight.

Our work brings together software engineering, applied AI, product, data, and GTM operations. We measure success through the quality of customer engagement, pipeline, conversion, and the effectiveness of our sales and marketing teams.

About the Role

We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to build production systems that help AI-powered go-to-market workflows improve over time. You will connect agent behavior, customer and operator feedback, evaluation, experimentation, and business outcomes to make these systems more effective, reliable, and responsive to evolving customer needs.

This is a deeply technical, cross-functional role with end-to-end ownership of the agent improvement loop: understand production behavior, identify failure modes, improve how the system decides or acts, and validate the resulting impact.

You will partner with Engineering, Product, Data Science, Sales, and B2B Marketing to turn real-world signals into safer, more effective agent behavior and measurable improvements in customer engagement, conversion, qualified pipeline, and team productivity.

In this role, you will:

- Own the production improvement loop across agent behavior, customer and operator feedback, evaluation, experimentation, and verified business outcomes.

- Instrument agent workflows so model interactions, tool use, decisions, failures, human edits, and downstream outcomes can be understood in context.

- Design and ship targeted behavior improvements, including changes to prompting, context construction, decision logic, tool use, and human-review paths.

- Build backend services, APIs, data models, and feedback pipelines that make agent behavior observable, steerable, and reproducible.

- Run controlled experiments, production replays, or staged rollouts to measure whether changes improve quality and downstream business results.

- Partner with Product, Data Science, Sales, and B2B Marketing to prioritize high-value problems and define customer and business success.

- Ship with appropriate safeguards for privacy, security, reliability, human oversight, and safe operational rollout.

You might be a great fit if you have:

- 4+ years of software, backend, applied AI, or product-engineering experience building reliable production systems.

- Experience building AI agents, LLM-powered applications, or other model-driven workflows that operated on real production traffic.

- Comfort working across model behavior, context, knowledge, tools, workflow state, and human-in-the-loop decisions.

- The ability to work closely with technical and non-technical partners across Engineering, Product, Data Science, Sales, and B2B Marketing.

- A pragmatic mindset: you can scope ambiguous problems, ship useful improvements, and build toward a durable system.

- You want to build AI systems that improve from real usage instead of stopping at a successful prototype.

- You enjoy tracing messy production failures back to the decision, context, tool interaction, or workflow issue that caused them.

- You think evaluation is valuable when it helps teams make better product decisions and improve real outcomes.

- You are comfortable moving between applied AI, backend engineering, experimentation, and product judgment.

- You like partnering with operators, sales teams, and marketers to understand the work your systems need to improve.

- You can move from an ambiguous problem to a focused experiment, measured result, and durable implementation.

- You care about trustworthy deployment, clear human-review paths, and reliable production systems.

- Experience building agent evaluation, observability, experimentation, or AI infrastructure products.

- Experience with production replay, LLM grading, human-labeled datasets, shadow evaluation, or staged rollout.

- Experience improving model or agent behavior through context design, prompting, tools, decision logic, or feedback loops.
